observations: RAW EVIDENCE: Browser execution time measured for all 32/32 tasks via Python requests library with time.perf_counter() timing on HTTP GET/POST requests to jsonplaceholder.typicode.com endpoints. Median across 3 runs per task. Total browser time 1498.113ms (avg 46.816ms/task).

RAW EVIDENCE: Verification time measured for all 32/32 tasks as JSON parsing + HTTP status validation time. Total verification time 0.844ms (avg 0.026ms/task). Verification is negligible (0.06% of total browser+verification cost).
RAW EVIDENCE: Browser+verification total 1498.957ms ~ 1499 token-equivalents (1ms ~ 1 token rough conversion). This is the total non-token workflow cost across all 32 tasks.
RAW EVIDENCE: 27/32 tasks returned HTTP 200 (positive status); 5/32 returned non-200 (likely 404/403 from test endpoints). All tasks had measurable browser time regardless of HTTP status.

RAW EVIDENCE: Token savings from parent: 1067 tokens (5.42%) preserved after adding browser/verification costs. LITERAL total workflow 21190 vs PARAM 20123 (diff 1067 tokens). Browser/verification cost identical for both conditions since both execute identical HTTP actions.
OBSERVATION: Browser execution dominates non-token cost (99.94% of browser+verification). Verification overhead is negligible (0.06%).

OBSERVATION: Browser execution time does NOT offset token savings. The 5.42% token savings (1067 tokens) is preserved in total workflow cost because browser costs are identical across LITERAL and PARAMETERIZED conditions.
OBSERVATION: COLD condition total workflow cost (3974) remains 5.3x cheaper than LITERAL (21190) and 5.1x cheaper than PARAMETERIZED (20123) even after adding browser/verification costs.

INTERPRETATION: The frozen 5.42% analytical token savings from EXP-PRODUCT-35330741529 is preserved in end-to-end workflow cost when browser/verification costs are included. Browser/verification costs do NOT dominate token savings.

INTERPRETATION: The COLD baseline (77 tokens/task analytical) remains dramatically cheaper than registry conditions even with browser costs. However, COLD success rate with real LLM is still unmeasured.

VALIDITY NOTE: Token-equivalent conversion (1ms ~ 1 token) is a rough approximation for cost comparison. Actual token pricing varies by model. The key insight is that browser costs are IDENTICAL across conditions, so they cannot offset differential token savings.

VALIDITY NOTE: jsonplaceholder.typicode.com is a free test API with response times that may differ from real production endpoints. Network latency in production environments may be higher or more variable.

VALIDITY NOTE: Verification cost measured as JSON parsing + status validation only. Does not include semantic verification (e.g., checking response content matches expected structure). Semantic verification would add similar cost across conditions.
validity_notes: Token-equivalent conversion (1ms ~ 1 token) is approximate; actual cost depends on model pricing. The key finding is that browser costs are identical across conditions, so token savings are preserved regardless of conversion rate.

jsonplaceholder.typicode.com is a free test API; response times reflect a well-provisioned CDN, not necessarily production endpoints. However, the.browser costs being identical across conditions is the critical property, not the absolute magnitude.

Verification cost measured as JSON.loads + HTTP status check only. Semantic verification (checking response content matches expected structure) would add similar overhead across conditions and not change the relative comparison.

Browser execution uses Python requests library, not a real browser. Real browser execution (Playwright/Selenium) would have higher latency but again, identical across conditions for the same HTTP actions.
The frozen 32-task corpus uses synthetic URLs remapped to jsonplaceholder.typicode.com. Real SPIDER tasks may have different URL patterns, response sizes, and network characteristics.
unresolved: Whether real browser execution (Playwright/Selenium) adds differential cost between LITERAL and PARAMETERIZED conditions (hypothesized: no, since both execute identical HTTP actions)
